question: Should OpenClaw sponsor an official Linux companion now, and if so should its first supported scope be a remote Control UI operator shell with direct/Tailscale connectivity while managed SSH tunneling and broader device-control parity remain deferred?
rationale: The remaining work requires a durable choice about supported desktop scope, remote authentication delivery, packaging, and the boundary between an operator client, a local Gateway, and an optional node.

options.title: Sponsor staged Linux shell
options.body: Approve a narrow remote-operator-first Linux companion that reuses canonical Gateway and Control UI contracts, with laptop-node support as a separate opt-in follow-up.

options.title: Prioritize Windows only
options.body: Keep Linux as community/plugin-adjacent work until an owner can fund and review its native packaging and security model.

options.title: Define cross-platform desktop plan
options.body: Establish one official Windows/Linux desktop architecture and ownership model before accepting further platform-specific implementation PRs.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged Linux shell
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow remote-operator-first Linux companion that reuses canonical Gateway and Control UI contracts, with laptop-node support as a separate opt-in follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion records their platform vision and priority guidance, making them the strongest available routing candidate.
